findings.reason: the first deliverable asks the node to name "the code path that left the local lane out of the candidate set", which is the shape of one attempt only; on the other three the local lane was in the set and excluded with a competence reason, so the plan sends the trace after a path that does not explain the evidence it cites, and cites a field the evidence does not carry.
findings.text: the Why says "Each reads:" and then "an empty `offered` set, with `exclusions` holding only three codex rows, each `reason_code: reserved-lane`, and no row for the local lane at all", but in `~/.config/reckon/crew/pick-timings.jsonl` only the 02:34:43Z attempt has that shape; the three earlier attempts (02:29:07Z, 02:30:52Z, 02:31:37Z) each carry eleven exclusion rows — four claude `reserved-lane`, two clive `context-fit`, one clive `competence`, three codex `reserved-lane` and one `native` `in-harness-backend` — so the local lane has a row, twice over, in three of the four records; and the log has no `offered` key in any of its 18,324 rows (`reckon/crew/picker/__init__.py:115` writes only `exclusions` and `estimated_context` for a refusal)

findings.reason: a node can deliver all four green cases, and "reverting the fix fails the first case" cannot bind, without the live refusal ever being reproduced, so the measure cannot show the defect was repaired.
findings.text: s23's four cases, as written, all hold on the unfixed code: `tests/test_an_oversize_node_reaches_a_reserved_lane.py:166` already offers an oversize node the reserved lane through the waiver (case 1's mechanism), `:257` already shows a lane excluded for another reason earns no waiver (case 3), `tests/test_one_rule_chooses_the_lane_for_an_oversized_request.py:155` already moves the request to the widest fitting lane on both paths (case 1's move), and `:240` already refuses with the shortfall when no lane fits (case 2); those 21 tests pass at this head (82672c0), and §15 and §16 both landed with case 4's named-lane rule; the done-when names no input from the records that the base revision gets wrong — nothing requires the local candidate to carry the `competence` exclusion or the local lane to be absent from the scan

findings.reason: a reader cannot tell which module owns which case, and the near-duplicate name makes the new test look like paid-for coverage of the existing one; the name should carry the input it reproduces rather than the outcome it hopes for.
findings.text: the done-when names the new test `tests/test_an_oversized_node_reaches_the_reserved_lane.py`, while `tests/test_an_oversize_node_reaches_a_reserved_lane.py` already exists and tests the same waiver, so the two modules differ only by an article and a suffix

findings.reason: the queue stores a section whose upstream has not landed as `awaiting-upstream`, so this entry delays s23 for a dependency it does not have and inverts the causality the plan's own Why describes.
findings.text: `plan-section-depends-on` declares `"s23": ["a-read-costs-what-changed#s6"]`, but that section is "Every hot path reads plan state through the memo" and s23's replay and tests consume none of it (they replay a `PickRequest` against the flight config and drive stub lane windows); §6 is also the node the incident is about — the one that could not be dispatched — so the declaration holds s23 behind the very section whose launch s23 exists to repair
